The Gstaad Palace reopens on 15 December 2026 for its 114th winter season, which runs until 7 March 2027. Over the summer, the hotel invested around €6.9 million (CHF 6.4 million) in works.

## What has changed

La Veranda has been folded into the restaurant Le Grand. Rooms have gained balconies and air conditioning. The spa and the GreenGo club have been redone, and so has the staff housing on the seventh floor, a detail that says a lot about how the house looks after its people.

The season's theme is the 1980s, a nod to the golden years of the GreenGo, the hotel's famous club.

## A family house

The Palace opened in December 1913. It is still owned by the Scherz family, now in its third generation, with Andrea Scherz as owner and general manager. He celebrated thirty years at the hotel in 2026, having started at reception in 1996.

The house counts 90 rooms and suites and, according to Andrea Scherz, more than 300 employees.

## A new chef in the kitchen

The other big change is in the kitchen. Franz W. Faeh, the long-serving culinary director, retired at the end of the summer of 2026. He is succeeded by Luca Gatti, who has been at the Palace for more than twenty years and becomes executive chef this winter, leading a team of 55. Gault&Millau rates the gourmet cuisine 16 points.

## The signal

In Gstaad, the competition is getting stronger, with new and renovated hotels coming back to the market. The Palace answers in the family way: a summer of works, a chef promoted from within, and investment in staff housing.

For hoteliers, it is a reminder that continuity can be a strategy. Promoting a 20-year team member and reinvesting every season are what keep a 1913 palace in the front row.

We wish the Gstaad Palace teams a wonderful 114th winter.
summary: The Gstaad Palace begins its 114th winter season on 15 December 2026, after around €6.9 million of works and with Luca Gatti as its new executive chef.
